answer: Latent Coordination Clustering: agents are embedded by their transaction counterparties, and a clustering pass flags dense subgraphs whose members share unusually few external links. A flagged cluster is frozen at the next dawn pending review, so an attacker must build a real external thread of unrelated counterparties for every identity, raising per-identity cost far above the value of a marginal fake. Residual ridge cases are re-clustered as history accrues.
